rationales: Family is a lower taxonomic rank than kingdom.
Order is a lower taxonomic rank than kingdom.
Class is a lower taxonomic rank than kingdom.
Kingdom is the largest taxonomic rank listed.
Chromosomes consist mainly of DNA associated with proteins.
RNA is not the main nucleic acid in chromosomes.
Lipids are not a main structural component of chromosomes.
Chromosomes are not composed mainly of RNA and lipids.
Glucose is a simple sugar, not the main structural material of the primary wall.
Cellulose is the principal structural component of the primary cell wall.
Fructose is not the main structural material of the primary wall.
Maltose is not the main structural material of the primary wall.
Endocytosis is the uptake of substances into a cell, not nuclear division.
Exocytosis is the release of substances from a cell, not nuclear division.
Karyokinesis is the division of the nucleus.
Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm.
A coenzyme is an organic cofactor that is generally loosely bound.
An apoenzyme is the protein part of an enzyme without its cofactor.
Cofactor is a general term and does not specifically mean tightly bound.
A tightly bound organic cofactor is called a prosthetic group.
Anaerobic breakdown of one glucose molecule yields a net gain of 2 ATP.
Four ATP are produced gross, but the net gain is only 2 ATP.
Six ATP are not gained as the net yield of anaerobic glycolysis.
Eight ATP are not gained as the net yield of anaerobic glycolysis.
The pancreas is a gland, but it is smaller than the liver.
The heart is an organ, not the body's largest gland.
The liver is the largest gland in the human body.
The gallbladder stores bile and is not a gland.
Xylem transports water and minerals rather than food substances.
Phloem transports food substances throughout the plant.
The epidermis is a protective outer tissue, not the food-transporting tissue.
The cortex is ground tissue and does not transport food throughout the plant.
The right atrium receives blood and is not the heart's strongest chamber.
The left atrium receives blood and is not the heart's strongest chamber.
The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs at lower pressure.
The left ventricle has the thickest wall and pumps blood throughout the body.
Glycolysis does not take place in the nucleus.
Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm.
Ribosomes make proteins and are not where glycolysis occurs.
Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm, not at the cell membrane.
Saliva contains amylase, which begins the digestion of starch.
Lipase digests fats and is not the principal enzyme in saliva.
Protease digests proteins and is not the principal enzyme in saliva.
Trypsin is a pancreatic protein-digesting enzyme, not a salivary enzyme.
Group O is the universal donor in the ABO system; O-negative is the universal red-cell donor.
Group A blood is not compatible with all ABO groups.
Group B blood is not compatible with all ABO groups.
Group AB is the universal recipient in the ABO system, not the universal donor.
Guard cells become flaccid when they lose water, causing stomata to close.
Chloride ion uptake can help promote opening, but stomata open when guard cells become turgid.
Turgid guard cells bow apart and open the stomatal pore.
Losing water makes guard cells flaccid and closes the stomata.
Al-Qanoon-fi-al-Tib is the famous medical work written by Bu-Ali-Sina.
Al-Nababat is not the famous medical work associated with Bu-Ali-Sina.
Al-Abil is not the famous medical work associated with Bu-Ali-Sina.
Al-Khail is not the famous medical work associated with Bu-Ali-Sina.
Water usually makes up more than 50–60% of protoplasm.
Water content commonly exceeds 60–70% in living protoplasm.
This range is too low as the general textbook estimate for protoplasm.
Water makes up about 60–90% of protoplasm in living organisms.
